paper_metadata.title: NCERT Class 7 Science Chapter 11 Model Test Paper
instructions: Section A contains 6 Objective Questions (4 MCQs + 2 Assertion-Reason) carrying 1 Mark each.
Section B contains 5 Short Answer Questions carrying 2 Marks each.
Section C contains 2 Long Answer Questions carrying 4 Marks each.
Section D contains 1 Case-Based Competency Question with 3 sub-questions carrying 2 Marks each.

questions.question_text: The image formed by a pinhole camera is always:
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (B). Explanation: Light rays traveling in straight lines cross through the pinhole, projecting a real inverted image on the screen.

questions.question_text: What is the key scientific indicator or property studied in Chapter 11?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option selection (A). Explanation: Derived from core terms.

questions.question_text: Which process occurs during the core phenomenon in Light: Shadows and Reflections?
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (C). Explanation: Standard curriculum observation.

questions.question_text: Select the correct definition for 'Law of Reflection':
options: A) 1. Angle of Incidence (i) = Angle of Reflection (r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct option (A). Explanation: Definition of Law of Reflection as stated in NCERT textbook.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): A pinhole camera forms a real and inverted image.
Reason (R): Light rays travel in straight lines through the narrow pinhole.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (A). Explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): The word 'AMBULANCE' is written laterally inverted on the bonnet of emergency vehicles.
Reason (R): Drivers ahead viewing the word in rearview mirrors see the correctly flipped image.
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 Mark for correct selection (A). Explanation: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_text: Differentiate between a shadow and a mirror image.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Shadow: Formed by light obstruction; dark region showing only object outline without color or detail. Mirror Image: Formed by light reflection; shows complete color, shape, and internal details of object.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying first key point; 1 Mark for second key point / clear explanation.

questions.question_text: List three mandatory requirements for shadow formation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. A source of light. 2. An opaque or translucent object to block light. 3. A screen or background surface behind the object where shadow falls.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for statement/formula; 1 Mark for calculation/application.
1 Mark for Point 1 of difference; 1 Mark for Point 2 of difference.

questions.question_text: If a light ray strikes a plane mirror surface at an angle of 35 degrees with the mirror surface, what is the angle of reflection?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Angle with mirror = 35 deg. Normal is at 90 deg. Angle of Incidence (i) = 90 - 35 = 55 deg. By Law of Reflection (i = r), Angle of Reflection (r) = 55 degrees.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying core cause; 1 Mark for explaining scientific effect.

questions.question_text: Correct the common misconception: 'Measuring angle of incidence from the mirror surface rather than from the normal.'. Provide the correct scientific fact.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Angle of incidence is ALWAYS measured between the incident light ray and the normal (perpendicular 90-degree line).
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for identifying error; 1 Mark for stating correct scientific fact.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer Questions - Diagrams & Processes)

questions.question_text: State the Laws of Reflection, draw a labeled ray diagram, and list four characteristics of images formed by plane mirrors.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Laws: 1. Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie on the same plane. Image Characteristics: 1. Virtual (cannot be caught on screen). 2. Erect (upright). 3. Same size as object. 4. Laterally inverted (left-right reversed). Image distance behind mirror equals object distance in front.
questions.breakdown: 1 Mark for introduction/definition; 2 Marks for detailed 4-point mechanism; 1 Mark for conclusion/example.

questions.question_text: Explain the structure and operation illustrated in 'Fig 11.6 / Ray Diagram of Reflection in Plane Mirror'. (i) Draw/describe the key components (Incident Ray, Reflected Ray, Normal (90 deg Line), Angle of Incidence (i), Angle of Reflection (r), Plane Mirror Surface). (ii) Detail the working mechanism and scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Component breakdown: Incident Ray, Reflected Ray, Normal (90 deg Line), Angle of Incidence (i), Angle of Reflection (r), Plane Mirror Surface.
Mechanism & Significance: Demonstrates Law of Reflection (i = r).
questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for labeling/describing key components accurately; 2 Marks for explaining working mechanism clearly.

question.case_scenario_text: A student constructs a periscope using a long cardboard tube and two plane mirrors.

sub_questions.question_text: At what angle must the two plane mirrors be fixed inside the periscope tube?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: The two plane mirrors must be fixed parallel to each other at an angle of 45 degrees relative to the length of the tube, allowing double reflection to view objects above line of sight.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for complete, accurate identification/explanation of the initial phenomenon.

sub_questions.question_text: Formulate a testable hypothesis or identify the chemical/physical principle.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for correct scientific reasoning and principle formulation.

sub_questions.question_text: What conclusion or practical precaution can be derived from this experimental observation?
sub_questions.marking_scheme_answer: Practical conclusion and safety/precautionary measure grounded in textbook guidelines.
sub_questions.breakdown: 2 Marks for valid evidence-based conclusion / real-world application.
